BayesForge (BF) is a Python library with R and Julia front-ends. All three need **Python ≥ 3.12**; the R and Julia packages create and manage their own Python environment, so R and Julia users do not need to install Python packages by hand.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## Python
```bash
pip install "BayesForge[cpu]"   # CPU (Linux, macOS, Windows)
pip install "BayesForge[gpu]"   # NVIDIA GPU (Linux and WSL2 only)
```

Check the installation:

```python
from BayesForge import bf
m = bf(platform="cpu")
```

## R
```r
install.packages("BayesForge")   # from CRAN

library(BayesForge)
setup_env(backend = "cpu")        # once: creates the 'BFR' Python environment
                                  # (use backend = "gpu" on Linux/WSL2 with an NVIDIA GPU)
```

Restart R, then:

```r
library(BayesForge)
m <- importBF(platform = "cpu")
```

`setup_env()` installs the `BayesForge` Python package and its dependencies (JAX, NumPyro, ArviZ) into a dedicated virtual environment, so it does not interfere with other Python installations. Run `setup_env()` again at any time to upgrade it.

## Julia
```julia
using Pkg
Pkg.add("PyBayesForge")          # from the Julia General registry
```

Then:

```julia
using PyBayesForge
m = importBF(platform = "cpu")    # first call installs the Python dependencies
```
:::

::: callout-note
* GPU support is only available on Linux and WSL2 systems with an NVIDIA GPU.
* If the R or Julia environment ends up in a broken state, delete it (R: `reticulate::virtualenv_remove("BFR")`; Julia: `PyBayesForge.delete_env()`) and run the setup step again.
:::
